title: Report input
description: Normalized campaign results. Produced from the pipeline's campaign bundle by threetears.evals.analysis.report_input_build.report_input (the kit's adapters/bundle_to_report.py is its first draft, reading a writer message). Statistics are copied through, never recomputed. A control-and-candidates campaign fills the core fields; the optional tasks, factors and configs, target_matrix and cells, confusion, human_pref, criteria and named strata carry what other comparison structures need (GENERATOR.md section 1). The model threetears.evals.analysis.report_input.ReportInput states the same fields, required sets and enums, and a test holds the two together. The r1-r4 references' own JSON is page-shaped synthetic data, not this schema; their report inputs are packages/evals/tests/fixtures/report_inputs/r1-r4/input.json.

floors.description: Each floor's status on each candidate.

bars.description: Each arm against each absolute bar.

guardrails.description: Each guardrail check, as the pipeline read it.

scoreboard.description: How each arm's trials came out on the lead aspect, by arm.

factors.description: A factorial grid's factors, in order.

lever_names.description: What a reader calls each lever an arm's settings key, by its id: the name the campaign stores for it, else the one its host declares. The one source every name of a lever reads (an arm's name computed from its levers, a setting, a factor, a lever-effect row); a lever absent here is printed as its id in words.

configs.description: Each arm's level of each factor.

confusion.description: Each label axis's confusion, by axis id.

failed_trials.description: The trials the run failed per aspect, arm and stratum, for any cause; none where the input does not count them.

case_overlap.description: For each two aspects, the cases both ran and the cases only one ran; none where the input does not hold the aspects' case ids.

apparatus.description: The rig each run was measured with, for each run that recorded one past a serial run pinning and declaring nothing; none where no run did, or the bundle carried none.

caveat_list.description: Every qualification of the answer, each once, typed; none on an input built before the list.

first_screen.description: The first screen's slots, as shown when the input was frozen; never part of the input's digest.

threshold.description: The threshold it was read against.

ApparatusConfound.description: An apparatus setting that may have varied between arms.

id.description: The arm's id, as every by-arm map keys it.

name.description: The campaign's alias for the arm.

short_name.description: The short name the campaign declares for the arm, printed in tight places; none computes one.

role.description: The control, or a candidate measured against it.

served_model.description: The model that served the arm's replies.

settings.description: Model plus every lever that differs from the control (the control lists every lever); a lever an arm leaves out has the control's value.

reasoning_ratio.description: The share of output spent reasoning.

description.description: What kind of candidate the arm is, in a few words.

arm_id.description: The id that names the arm apart from its label; names one cell where the arm is split.

cell.description: The one cell the arm id names, where the arm is split over several.

spelling.description: The levers code spelled the arm's computed name from, each with its level, in order.

identity.description: Whether the arm is one thing, a state per coordinate.

Arm.description: One arm: what it ran and the part it plays.

name.description: What a reader calls the aspect.

margin.description: The non-inferiority margin, in points; none declared.

asked.description: Whether the campaign's question asks about it.

exploratory_measures.description: Measures read on the aspect but not asked about.

readings.description: Each candidate's reading against the control.

depth.description: How deeply each arm ran it, by arm.

pairs.description: A choice's pair readings on the aspect.

scoreboard.description: How each arm's trials came out on this aspect, by arm; none on the lead aspect (the first asked, else the first), whose scoreboard is the input's own.

description.description: How the aspect is graded, in a sentence or two.

graded_by.description: Whether a judge grades the aspect (with any checks beside it) or checks in code alone do.

pass_rule.description: How a trial on the aspect passes: its criteria, threshold, counted dimensions and checks; none where the input does not say.

margin_informative.description: Whether any margin a reader could plausibly hold changes a reading on the aspect.

looks.description: How often the aspect's test was looked at, against how often it planned to be. Derived from stored facts about the campaign (its launches, membership, re-judges), never an input the author gave, so never part of the input's digest; the plan it is read against (`AspectDesign.planned_looks`) is.

Aspect.description: One aspect the campaign read: its question and each candidate's reading against the control.

aspect.description: The aspect it is read on.

measure.description: What the bar is read on.

bar.description: The threshold, in the measure's units.

value.description: The arm's value on the measure.

interval.description: The interval the status was read on.

BarRead.description: One arm against one absolute bar: met, missed or unclear, as the pipeline read it.

aspects.description: The two aspects' ids, in the input's aspect order.

only_first.description: The cases only the first ran.

only_second.description: The cases only the second ran.

CaseOverlap.description: Whether two aspects ran the same cases: the distinct cases each ran, by their stored ids, shared or not.

confounds.description: Each confound and what it means.

latency.description: Why latency is not compared, when it is not.

unfinished.description: What stopped each run that did not finish, a sentence each in code's words, then what the readings cover: what a page opens with in place of a verdict. Empty where every run completed.

Caveats.description: Every disclosure the flag and the method section may need.

per_arm.description: Each arm's figures in the cell: arm, then measure.

Cell.description: One cell of the target matrix and each arm's figures in it.

levels.description: Each factor's level id, by factor id.

Config.description: The level of each factor one arm ran.

labels.description: The labels, in row and column order.

unit.description: row_percent: each row sums to 100; count: observations.

ConfusionTable.description: Where one label axis's predictions went: rows are the expected label, columns the predicted one.

measure.description: The measure or judged dimension, by key.

aspect.description: The aspect it is read on.

verdict.description: improved, regressed, equivalent, not_separated or untested.

delta.description: The arm minus the control, in the measure's units; none when untested.

interval.description: The corrected interval on the delta; none when untested.

confounds.description: Confounds on the contrast, by dimension.

reason.description: Why it is untested or not separated, in one sentence.

n_cases.description: The cases the test read on the arm's side, each one mean over its repeats: when paired, the cases both arms ran.

control_n_cases.description: The cases the test read on the control's side, where they differ from n_cases (an unpaired test).

paired.description: Whether the test paired the arms case by case; none where it was not tested.

pairing_r.description: The arms' correlation across the paired cases: how much pairing narrowed the interval.

state.description: The contrast's state where it is not counted, with its reason; none reads counted.

baseline.description: The control's mean over the cases the test paired: what the delta is a change from.

baseline_n_cases.description: The cases that baseline is the mean of.

family.description: The family the contrast was corrected in, by id.

delta_note.description: Why the delta is not the difference of the two means printed beside it, where it is not.

corrected.description: The contrast as what its judge was checked against would read it: a check's result, never a second verdict.

aa.description: The A/A check covering the contrast: identical arms read on the same reading.

Contrast.description: One multiple-comparison-corrected contrast of an arm against the control on one measure.

aspect.description: The aspect whose contrasts it corrects.

merit_axes.description: The declared merit priority; empty when no rule ranks the axes.

correction.description: The correction method, e.g. holm, none.

disclosure.description: What the correction means, in plain words.

ContrastFamily.description: One family of contrasts corrected together.

kind.description: gate: an option failing it is out; floor and bar: they warn; guardrail: a standing must-not-worsen.

measure.description: The measure, judged dimension or aspect it reads, by key.

direction.description: higher_is_better: the value must be at least the threshold; lower_is_better: at most.

threshold.description: The threshold, in the measure's units.

scope.description: overall: the arm's overall value; each_task: every task's value; each_cell: every cell's.

task.description: The one task the criterion applies within.

standing.description: Whether it is standing policy rather than this campaign's.

aspect.description: The aspect whose figures it reads, by id: the lead aspect's are the by-arm maps, any other's its by_aspect figures; none: the lead aspect's (the first asked, else the first).

Criterion.description:
A declared threshold: a gate, floor, bar or guardrail on one measure.

A criterion states the rule; one gate function applies it, so the page, the options and any explore control
cannot disagree. ``floors`` and ``bars`` carry the pipeline's own statuses where it read them.

repeats_per_case.description: Fewest, mean and most repeats a case got.

Depth.description: How deeply one arm ran an aspect.

stratum.description: The stratum or task it falls in.

reason.description: Why it failed: the judge's reason or a note.

excerpt.description: The end of the reply, or what the arm produced.

reasons.description: Each judged dimension's reason for the trial, by dimension, the primary's among them; none where the input does not carry them.

Example.description: One trial shown as an example, usually a failure.

id.description: The factor's id, as configs and settings key it.

ordered.description: Whether the levels are points on one scale, so a line may be drawn across them.

Factor.description: One factor of a factorial grid, or one axis of a target matrix, with its levels in order.

aspect.description: The aspect the slice ran on.

stratum.description: The stratum or task it falls in; none for none.

failed.description: The trials of the slice its pass rule failed, for any cause.

FailedTrials.description: How many trials of one slice of the run failed, for any cause, as the scoreboard's `failed` counts them.

aspect.description: The aspect it is read on.

reading.description: The rate that decided the status.

speaks_for.description: The rate the floor speaks for.

interval.description: The interval the status was read on.

worst_drop.description: The largest drop the interval allows, in points.

short_by.description: How far an unclear floor is from held, in points.

FloorRead.description: One floor on one candidate: held, broken or unclear, as the pipeline read it.

read_id.description: The blind read the ratings come from.

person.description: Who rated, where the read records it.

test.description: The test the preference was read by.

verdict.description: The contrast verdict it comes to.

HumanPreference.description: Blind side-by-side ratings of the control against one arm.

calibration_ratings.description: Human ratings the judge was calibrated on.

agreement.description: The judge's agreement with those ratings.

level.description: The confidence level of the intervals per_arm carries.

by_aspect.description: Each other aspect's figures, by aspect then arm; per_arm is the lead aspect's (the first asked, else the first).

checks.description: The judge's checks: what it was checked against, on what sample, with what result.

instrument.description: The claim criterion this reading is one of: a rate or a share of claims, never a score.

lost.description: On a claim reading: the cells its criterion lost, by arm, where any did.

pending.description: On a claim reading: the cells whose tally waits on its stored grade, by arm: no loss, not yet known.

unread.description: On a reading the host derives from a claim criterion: the cells its claim reader could not read, by arm; no loss, read once the reader is fixed and the run re-measured.

silent.description: On a claim reading: the cells whose candidate said nothing, by arm; no loss, and in no mean, since a cell with nothing said has no denominator.

web_skipped.description: On a claim reading: the cells whose web check skipped a claim past its budget, by arm; each skipped claim reads unverifiable, never false.

web_lost.description: On a claim reading: the cells whose web step failed, by arm, a cause apart from the budget; its undecided claims read unverifiable, never false.

Judged.description: One judged dimension: its judge and each arm's mean.

criterion.description: What was set: aspect, control, margin, floor, gate.

name.description: Which one, where several could be.

aspect.description: A floor's aspect, by its id.

reading.description: The reading a floor names; none for a floor on every pass rate.

LateCriterion.description: A criterion set after the results were visible.

Level.description: One level of a factor, axis or bin.

unit.description: Its unit, e.g. usd (dollars per reply), pct, ms, s, usd_per_1k (dollars per 1,000 of what the label counts: Cost per 1k conversations), usd_per_1m (dollars per 1,000,000 of what the label counts), share (a fraction on 0 to 1, read as a rate in percent: 0.78 reads 78%). A page prints a counted cost per what its label names after the count, and says the count is not stated where the label names none.

merit_axis.description: The merit axis it counts toward.

grade.description: For a rate or score over graded cases, what one case's grade is: a pass or fail, a point on a scale, or a class label right or wrong.

level.description: The confidence level of the intervals per_arm carries.

bins.description: The bins a distribution's shares fall in, in order.

minimum.description: The least the measure can be, where the test set fixes it (a gold call count).

by_aspect.description: Each other aspect's figures, by aspect then arm; per_arm is the lead aspect's (the first asked, else the first).

Measure.description: One measure: what it means and each arm's figure on it.

question.description: The question the campaign asked, in its own words.

behavior.description: The system or behavior under test.

kind.description: The pipeline kind, e.g. change (control + candidates).

kind_means.description: What the kind recommends, in one sentence.

synthetic.description: Whether the data is made up for an example.

volume_per_month.description: Replies or calls per month, when the host declares it; enables monthly cost.

Meta.description: What the campaign was, as the masthead and the method section name it.

arms.description: The two arms' ids, first then second, in the campaign's arm order.

change.description: The first arm minus the second, in points.

interval.description: The interval on the change, in points.

ahead.description: The arm shown ahead; none when neither is.

confirmatory.description: Whether the pair answers the asked question.

passed.description: Each arm's passes, as 'k of n'.

state.description: The pair's state where it is not counted, with its reason; none reads counted.

PairRead.description: Two arms of a choice on one aspect: the difference between them, and which one is shown ahead.

criteria.description: What a trial is held to: goal_checks (every goal check), rubric (every counted judged dimension at the threshold), both, or neither.

threshold.description: The 1 to 5 level a counted judged dimension must reach.

label.description: The pass^k label every surface prints for this rule.

dimensions.description: The judged dimensions that count, by key: the capability ones.

boundary.description: The judged dimensions that do not count, by key: guardrails, decided apart.

checks.description: The checks that fail a trial on their own, by measure key: goal checks, a label match and pass/fail scorers.

named_checks.description: Each check in `checks` that is no goal check, as the rule names it: the measure's reader name and the value it must hold for the trial to pass (`Never topped up is false`); the other value fails the trial. Goal checks are named on the page's glossary, so the rule sums them up as every goal check.

no_criterion.description: Trials that passed with nothing to fail them, across every arm.

PassRule.description: How code decides whether one trial on an aspect passed, read off the bundle it was decided in.

common_depth.description: The fewest runs any arm gave a shared case.

shares_no_case.description: Whether the arms share no case at that depth.

unmeasured_for.description: Arms pass^k is not measured for.

said.description: What the pipeline says about it.

PassK.description: Where pass^k is compared, and at what depth.

own_half_width.description: Each arm's own half-width, by arm.

limited_by.description: The arm whose noise limits the interval.

between_case_share.description: The share of the variance that lies between cases.

means.description: What the decomposition means, in one sentence.

Precision.description: What limits a reading's interval at its nominal level.

prefers_control.description: The share of ratings preferring the control, percent.

PreferenceRow.description: Blind human preference in one slice.

confidence.description: How sure the earlier campaign was.

PriorInsight.description: An insight an earlier campaign recorded.

reading.description: The pipeline's verdict, e.g. within_margin, regressed, not_separated.

change.description: The arm minus the control, in points.

within_interval.description: The interval on the change at the nominal level, low then high, in points: what within_margin is read on. None where the aspect declares no margin.

gain_interval.description: The interval on the change at gain_confidence, low then high, in points: what a gain is read on.

margin.description: The margin the reading was read against, in points.

control_passed.description: The control's passes, as 'k of n'.

arm_passed.description: The arm's passes, as 'k of n'.

cases.description: The paired cases the interval rests on.

confirmatory.description: Whether the reading answers the asked question.

state.description: The reading's state where it is not counted, with its reason; none reads counted.

flip_margin.description: The margin at which the reading would read the other way, in points.

Reading.description: One arm's reading on an aspect: its change from the control, with the interval it was read on.

strict_output.description: Whether the request enforced every parameter it carried.

RequestSettings.description: What a role's calls were asked for: the output cap, the reasoning asked, and whether every parameter was enforced.

arm.description: The arm it ran, by id; none for a run the design placed in no arm.

aspect.description: The aspect it ran, by id.

judges.description: The model each judged dimension was asked of; none where not recorded.

judge_asked.description: What every judge call was asked for; none where not recorded.

judge_temperature.description: The temperature judge calls were asked at; none where not recorded.

simulator.description: The simulated user's model; none where none was pinned.

measure_latency.description: Whether latency was declared under test; none where nothing was declared.

arm_schedule.description: How the arm shared time with the other arms; none where not recorded.

cell_concurrency.description: How many of the run's cells executed at once; 1 is serial.

execution_modes.description: The run's results by the execution mode each recorded.

rubric_scales.description: The scale each rubric dimension was answered on.

disclosure.description: What the launching host disclosed about the launch; none where it disclosed nothing.

RunRig.description: The rig one run of one arm was measured with, as the run recorded it at launch.

values.description: Each disclosed value by the host's name for it.

statements.description: What the host states, in its own words.

Disclosure.description: What the launching host disclosed about one run's launch, as it stated it: values by its own names, and its statements of how the run was measured. Shown, never compared: it splits no rig and names no confound.

usable.description: Trials that produced a usable measurement.

test_cost_usd.description: What the arm's trials cost, dollars.

unanswered.description: The arm's unanswered calls by usage role, for each role that counted them; none where no role did (not counted, never none).

pricing.description: How the arm's cost was priced: its price sources, serving providers and priced calls; none where the input does not say.

cost.description: The arm's one cost reading, the fallback from cost per reply decided once.

state.description: The row's state where its passes and failures are not counted, with its reason: withheld where the cells keep the arm apart on a coordinate, which it names; none reads counted.

ScoreboardRow.description: How one arm's trials came out.

note.description: What it lost, and what that does to its rates.

ShortRun.description: A run that produced fewer usable measurements than it was asked for.

mean.description: The mean, in the measure's units.

ci.description: The interval on the mean, low then high.

half_width.description: The interval's half-width, where only that is given.

sem.description: The standard error of the mean.

change.description: The arm minus the control, where only that is given.

shares.description: The share in each of the measure's bins, percent.

spread.description: The spread of the arm's per-case values, in the measure's units.

no_variation.description: The one value every case took, where the cases did not vary.

state.description: The interval's state where it is not counted, with its reason; none reads counted.

Stat.description: One arm's figure on one measure: a mean with its spread, a latency's percentiles, or a distribution.

aspect.description: The aspect whose cases it slices.

dimension.description: The stratification it belongs to, when the input holds more than one.

cost_multiplier.description: Its cost per reply relative to the average.

per_arm.description: Each arm's figures in the stratum: arm, then measure or dimension.

Stratum.description: One stratum: a slice of the cases and each arm's figures in it.

TargetMatrix.description: Two label axes whose product is the cells a classifier is graded in.

description.description: What it covers, in a sentence.

share.description: Its share of traffic, 0 to 1; 0 for a test category.

routable.description: Whether its traffic can be routed to its own arm.

cross_cutting.description: Whether it occurs inside every other task.

per_arm.description: Each arm's figures in the task: arm, then measure or dimension.

Task.description:
A named slice of the work, with each arm's figures in it.

A routable task's traffic can go to its own arm; a cross-cutting one occurs inside every other task, so an arm
serving any traffic must pass it.

sources.description: Each price source its priced calls name (RoleUsage.price_source), sorted.

providers.description: Each provider its model calls name as serving them (RoleUsage.served_provider, else RoleUsage.provider, on every role but external), sorted; empty where none does: not recorded.

providers_in_part.description: Some of its model calls named no provider beside calls that named one: providers names who served part of them, and the rest are not recorded.

tool_providers.description: Each provider its tool calls name (RoleUsage.provider on an external row, such as a web-search API), sorted: tool spend its cost counts, never a provider of the model.

calls.description: The calls its cost counts; none where a row did not count its.

priced_calls.description: Those of them a price was observed for; none where a row did not count its calls.

Pricing.description: How one arm's cost was priced: what priced its calls, who served them, and how many of them were priced.

retried.description: Calls a forced tool choice was refused on, answered unforced in the same call: attempts and latency, never a failure; none where nothing counted them.

lost.description: Calls sent and never answered, so their turn ended in error: failures the arm's trials already count; none where nothing counted them.

reasons.description: The calls each reason accounts for, by word.

calls.description: The answered calls beside them, which the cost counts; none where uncounted.

share.description: Retried and lost as a share of every call sent, 0 to 1; none where uncounted.

uncounted.description: Trials whose calls in the role counted none, absent from the sums: 'at least'.

Unanswered.description: One role's calls of one arm's trials that went unanswered, beside the arm's cost and never inside it.

ArmIdentity.description:
Whether an arm is one thing, a state per coordinate of :data:`Coordinate`; a coordinate left out was not
read.

served_model.description: Whether one model answered the arm's candidate calls.

measure_definition.description: Whether each host measure's values were read under one definition, by measure.

template.description: Whether the arm's runs ran one revision of one template.

rig.description: Whether the arm's runs were measured under one rig: one measurement context.

CallRead.description: The call on a campaign, as of the freeze: the arm decided, who decided, and what has moved since.

made_by.description: A person or a model; none where the call recorded none.

model.description: The model that made it, by id.

on_behalf_of.description: Who a model made it for.

runs_joined_since.description: Runs that joined the evidence after the call.

identity_changed.description: Whether the evidence's fingerprint differs from the one the call was read against.

CaveatEntry.description:
One row of the one caveat list: a qualification of the answer, typed so code ranks it without reading a word.

Every first-screen qualification is one of these. ``against`` and ``criterion`` say what a caveat about an
instrument's check was checked against and on which criterion, which is what lets a check against people silence a
check against a model, and what ranks a judge checked against a model only.

id.description: The caveat's stable id, as a report document names it.
id.title: Id

kind.description: The id's kind, which decides its class.
kind.title: Kind

class.description: What it does to the answer, A to E; none for a method-reach kind.
class.title: Class

state.description: The non-counted state that raised it, where one did.
state.title: State

reason.description: That state's reason, or the reason a check is not met.
reason.title: Reason

coordinate.description: The coordinate a split or an unrecorded identity names.
coordinate.title: Coordinate

arms.description: The arm ids it touches; empty for all.
arms.title: Arms

readings.description: The readings it is scoped to, each '<aspect>/<measure>'; empty for the whole report.
readings.title: Readings

asked.description: Whether it touches an asked aspect: one of its readings is on one, or it is scoped to the whole report and the report asks about one.
asked.title: Asked

deciding.description: Whether the answer turns on a reading it names: a class E caveat reaches the first screen only where it does.
deciding.title: Deciding

immaterial.description: True once code proved it changes no answer; none where code cannot say.
immaterial.title: Immaterial

subsumed_by.description: The caveat that silences it, by id.
subsumed_by.title: Subsumed By

against.description: For a caveat about an instrument's check: what the instrument was checked against.
against.title: Against

criterion.description: For such a caveat: the criterion the check decides; for a gate cleared on a point estimate or a borderline figure: the gate, by id.
criterion.title: Criterion

same_family.description: For a check against a model: whether the model is of a candidate's family.
same_family.title: Same Family

check.description: For a caveat about an instrument's check: the check's result. Only a result that decides (met or not met) speaks for the instrument, so only such a check against people silences one against a model.
check.title: Check

runs.description: The runs it is about, by id; empty for none named.
runs.title: Runs

cases.description: The cases the readings it names rest on, where one count says it.
cases.title: Cases

looks.description: For a caveat on looks: the aspect's looks, planned and taken, or that they were not recorded (`Aspect.looks`).

false_separation.description: For a caveat on looks: per test the aspect's readings are read by, a reference false-separation rate from a simulation of that test, plan and count, with the setting it was simulated in, or why none is quoted. A reference figure, never this campaign's own rate, which is not known and can be higher. Empty where the looks counted are a lower count (more may have been taken, so no row is the situation's: the count is shown alone), or were not recorded.

CaveatEntry.title: CaveatEntry

FalseSeparation.description:
A reference figure for one test the aspect's readings are read by: how often a test with no true difference
separated at some look in a simulation of that test, plan and count, in the setting stated beside it
(:func:`~threetears.evals.analysis.significance.looks_false_separation`). It is never this campaign's own rate,
which is not known, and it is no limit on it: a campaign launched smaller, extended by more cases a step, or
reading several claims at once can err more. For a claim of held (one tail) it is the two-sided separation rate.

test.description: The test the reference simulates: bounded or t.

rate.description: The rate a reference simulation of this test, plan and count measured, as a share, in the setting beside it; never this campaign's rate. None where none is quoted (``unquoted`` says why).

upper.description: The reference simulation's own uncertainty about ``rate``: the one-sided 97.5% Wilson upper confidence limit from its replicates. Nothing about this campaign's error. None with no rate.

row.description: The row of `significance.FALSE_SEPARATION` the rate is read from; None with no rate.

looks.description: The looks the reference rate is for.

setting.description: What the reference simulated, in one line: a single contrast, the test, the per-case values, the launch and the extends. None where no row measured the situation.

launched.description: The cases the simulated first looks read; empty where no row measured it.

largest_step.description: The most cases one later look added in the simulation; None where no row did.

unquoted.description: Why no rate is quoted: not_measured (no row for this test, plan and count) or outside_setting (the aspect's own first-look cases or largest step, from stored facts, fall outside the simulated setting, so the reference does not cover it). None with a rate.

instrument.description: What was checked: a judge by its dimension, a reviewer by its id, or the rig.

criterion.description: The criterion the check decides, where it names one.

against_id.description: The model it was checked against, by id.

same_family_as.description: The arms whose candidate model is of the family of the model checked against.

sample.description: Whether the items it was read on were drawn at random, chosen, or no sample stands behind it.

read_id.description: The blind read the sample is, by id.

reason.description: Why the result is not met, where a shared reason says it.

coordinate.description: The coordinate an unrecorded identity names, where that is the reason.

state.description: Where the check could not be made at all (both sides replayed a recording): not available, why.

lean.description: The instrument's lean toward one arm.

lean_untested.description: The arms, by key, a lean across arms was not tested on, each for lean_untested_reason: so a met check never reads as one that ruled a lean out on them.
lean_untested.title: Lean Untested

lean_untested_reason.description: Why the lean was not tested on those arms: too_few, their answered claims too few to read a rate.
lean_untested_reason.title: Lean Untested Reason

half_width.description: The half-width the check was read at.

reading.description: The reading a check of the rig covers.

covers_arms.description: The arms a check of the rig covers.

Corrected.description: A check's result on one judged contrast: the contrast as what the judge was checked against would read it.

state.description: Its state where it is not counted.

lean.description: The judge's lean the correction removes.

labelled_cases.description: Cases both the judge and the other reader read.

identical_cases.description: Of those, the cases they read alike.

read_id.description: The blind read the correction rests on.

FirstScreen.description:
What a report's first screen holds beside the answer, in four fixed slots, as typed values and no text.

The gate (can this be read at all), the trust slot's reasons (at most three caveats, ranked, with the count past
them), and the call. The answer slot holds no field: it is the verdicts and warnings the input already carries.
Computed by one function over the caveat list
(:func:`~threetears.evals.analysis.first_screen.first_screen`), and left out of the input's digest, since it is a
function of the rest of the input and of a call that may be made after the freeze.

gate.description: What stopped the read; none when the campaign can be read.

reasons.description: The ranked caveats shown, by id.
reasons.title: Reasons

remainder.description: The eligible caveats past the three shown.
remainder.title: Remainder

open_report_caveats.description: Every open report-wide caveat, shown or not.
open_report_caveats.title: Open Report Caveats

called_arms.description: The arms code's own read of the options calls: what ranks a caveat on them.
called_arms.title: Called Arms

call.description: The call, where one was made.

steps.description: What would change each reason shown, in their order; under a gate, what would lift it.
steps.title: Steps

FirstScreen.title: FirstScreen

Gate.description: What stops a campaign from being read at all; a campaign that can be read has none.

fewest_cases.description: For too few cases: the fewest usable cases an arm read holds.
fewest_cases.title: Fewest Cases

waiting.description: The open report-wide caveats waiting below the gate.
waiting.title: Waiting

Gate.title: Gate

ended_because.description: Why it ended, in its record's own words; never one of the shared reasons.

Looks.description:
How often a reading's test was looked at, against how often it planned to be.

A look is an occasion on which the contrast's test could have been read again on more or different evidence
(:func:`~threetears.evals.analysis.significance.looks_taken`): the first, once both arms held a result; then each
launch whose results changed what the test reads, each run that joined or left, each re-measure and each re-judge
made after it. ``taken`` is the most any one contrast of the aspect has had. It is exact where every such fact is
stored, and a lower bound (``lower_bound``) where one is not: a run that left with no result recorded, an archived
or unresolved member, a result with no ordered time, or re-judges, which are stored per result, so passes over
different results cannot be told apart.

**Looks were not recorded** (``recorded`` false) where a member run's joining was never recorded: it joined before
durable 17.3 recorded membership. The occasions its stored results give are then artifacts of how the runs were
stored (each arm launched alone, one group of cases after another), not occasions on which a reading could have
been taken, and runs joined in one write are dated each by its own launch: the count could be too high or too low,
so it is neither a bound above nor a bound below, and it is not given as looks. ``evidence_changes`` gives that
count as what it is: how many times the stored evidence changed. Where looks were recorded since (a run joined,
left, was launched after it joined, re-measured or re-judged after the first comparison), ``taken`` is the first
comparison plus those, a true lower count (``lower_bound``): at least that many looks since looks were recorded,
and earlier ones not recorded. Where none were, ``taken`` is None.

planned.description: The looks the design plans, where the plan was declared before the first look; None where none was, or where it was declared after (``late_plan``).

taken.description: The looks taken. Where looks were not recorded (``recorded`` false): the looks recorded since, counting the first comparison, a lower count; None where none were.

plannable.description: Whether the campaign was created once looks were counted, so its design could have declared them. False for an earlier campaign: its stored verdicts do not move, and its looks qualify the method only.

lower_bound.description: Whether ``taken`` is a lower bound: a fact a look is counted by is not stored, so more were taken.

recorded.description: Whether looks were recorded: false where a member run joined before durable 17.3 recorded membership, so the looks before are not counted; ``taken`` is then only the looks recorded since, a lower count, or None.

evidence_changes.description: Where looks were not recorded: how many times the stored evidence of a contrast changed (its runs' launches, re-measures and re-judges as stored), context and not a count of looks. None where they were.

launched.description: The fewest cases any contrast of the aspect read at its first look. None where not counted.

largest_step.description: The most cases one later occasion added to any contrast of the aspect. None where not counted.

tests.description: The tests the aspect's readings are read by, sorted: ``bounded`` (a pass rate, a judged score, a guardrail) and ``t`` (a mean, a measure's score, a cost per reply). What a caveat on looks quotes a measured rate for.

late_plan.description: The looks a plan declared after the first look named (or over runs that held results before it was declared): read as no plan, since the looks it would count were already taken. None where no plan was declared late.

NextExperiment.description:
What recording one dimension would buy, in pooled observations.

Both counts are :attr:`Cell.n_observations`, maxed or summed over the cells in question, and
are named for it: a replication claim reads a run's ``k_runs``, never these.

The mitigation that keeps a conservative merge from being pure refusal. Generated
mechanically — no model is asked — because it is arithmetic: these observations already
share a variant, and the only thing keeping them in separate cells is a dimension nobody
wrote down. Recording it either merges them or proves they never should have merged, and
both answers are worth more than the current silence.

variant_key.description: The variant whose pooling is being held back.
variant_key.title: Variant Key

n_observations_now.description: The largest `n_observations` among the cells this one recording would merge — the baseline the gain is measured against. Scoped to those cells rather than to the whole variant, because a variant-wide baseline would compare this merge's result against a cell it cannot reach and report a real gain as none.
n_observations_now.title: N Observations Now

n_observations_if_recorded.description: The `n_observations` those cells reach together once the dimension is recorded AND turns out to agree. The optimistic branch, deliberately: the pessimistic one — they disagree and stay apart — needs no action, so the number worth showing is the one that says what is at stake.
n_observations_if_recorded.title: N Observations If Recorded

observation_ids.description: The observations missing the dimension — where the recording has to happen, sorted.
observation_ids.title: Observation Ids

NextExperiment.title: NextExperiment

RemedyStep.description:
What would change one first-screen reason, or what stops a campaign being read: the one act that closes it, as
a value a person reads and an agent can take.

Where an action of the engine's catalogue takes the step, ``action`` names it, ``calls`` holds each call of it the
step makes, every argument named and typed as the action's own parameters (a step that adds cases passes its
planned size as the count of new cases), and ``needs`` names the parameters the step cannot fill from what the
caveat holds, which the taker supplies to every call. A launch repeats the set-up of the arms it runs: what the
reading holds of it is filled, and ``as_launched`` names the rest, each set as the arms' runs were launched, except
the dimensions ``alike`` names, held at one value on every call; ``call_arms`` says which arms each call runs.
Where one action's calls do not finish the act, ``then`` holds the calls that do, in order, each of the same
shape: a launch's runs joined to the campaign it reads, the runs a re-run replaces taken out of it, and for a
confirmation the campaign created first; ``after`` names each argument that only an earlier call's result holds.
A step ships a sequence only where following it, through the real actions on a fixture campaign, has been shown
to do what it says; ``limits`` states, typed, what following it cannot guarantee, and a re-run no sequence has
been shown to lift makes no call and says so (``no_action`` ``lift_not_shown``).
Where the step is more evidence, ``planned_cases`` is its size, read from the figure it would settle and stated
before it runs, never "until it separates"; where no size can be read, ``unsized`` says why and the step makes no
call, so it is never taken open-ended. Where no action takes it, ``no_action`` says why. A step that spends names
the action that prices it first; code never takes a step.

closes.description: The caveat it answers, by id; none for the gate's. A step whose first call is campaign_create closes nothing on this report: the caveat stays raised here, and the confirmation is read in the campaign it creates (limits: this_report_stays_flagged).
closes.title: Closes

action.description: The catalogue action that takes it; none where a host or a person acts.
action.title: Action

calls.description: Each call of the action the step makes, its arguments by the action's own parameter names; empty where no action takes it.
calls.title: Calls

needs.description: The action's parameters no call fills, by its own names, which the taker supplies to every call.
needs.title: Needs

as_launched.description: For a launch: the parameters that set an arm up which the reading holds no value for, by the action's own names; the taker sets each as the runs of the arms it launches were launched, never to its default, or the new runs are not more of those arms. The one exception is a dimension alike names, which the taker sets to one value on every call.
as_launched.title: As Launched

alike.description: For a re-run that balances a confound: each apparatus dimension the confound is in, by its apparatus_settings key, which the taker sets to one value on every call of the launch, never as each arm was launched: the arms then differ only in what is compared.
alike.title: Alike

call_arms.description: For a launch: the arms each call runs, by id, in the calls' order; empty where the reading does not hold the arms' runs.
call_arms.title: Call Arms

after.description: For a call that follows another of the step: each parameter only an earlier call's result holds, and which: launched_runs, the run ids job_poll names on the step's launch job once its runs start (run_ids); launched_control_run, the one of them the control arm's model ran, named as soon as job_poll names it and before any result is scored, or the campaign reads its control as named late; created_campaign, the id the step's campaign_create returned.
after.title: After

then.description: The calls that finish the act after this step's own, in order, each of one action and of this shape: the runs a launch makes joined to the campaign (campaign_runs_add), the runs a re-run replaces taken out (campaign_runs_remove), the control named in a new campaign (campaign_update). Empty on a call that follows another.
then.title: Then

arms.description: The arms it is about, by id; empty for all.
arms.title: Arms

runs.description: The runs it is about, by id; empty for none named.
runs.title: Runs

planned_cases.description: For more evidence: the cases to add per arm named (on fresh cases, the cases to run), read from the figure it would settle, planned before it runs, so that once the runs it launches are in the campaign that reads it, a design of that size clears the line the caveat is lifted by, on the interval it is lifted by, at least four times in five if the truth is today's estimate. It counts cases the launch keeps and did not reuse (limits: axis_may_not_generate), and holds only for arms launched in one call with the control (limits: unpaired_arms). For a step whose first call is campaign_create, the line is the one the created campaign reads, never this report's.
planned_cases.title: Planned Cases

unsized.description: For more evidence no size can be read for: why. Such a step makes no call.
unsized.title: Unsized

size_bias.description: Why the planned size is known to be too small, where it is: picked_best_of_n, read from the pick's own estimate, which reads high because the pick was the best of several, so fewer than four designs in five of that size clear.
size_bias.title: Size Bias

declared_look.description: Whether taking it reads the same readings again with the cases it adds: one more look at them, stated before it is taken. The looks are counted: past the aspect's plan (past the first with none), or within it where keeping the plan is not shown, the reading after it carries a caveat on looks, with a reference false-separation rate from a simulated setting.
declared_look.title: Declared Look

results_needed.description: For a check: how many more results it needs before it can decide.
results_needed.title: Results Needed

recording.description: What recording an unrecorded coordinate would pool, cell by cell.
recording.title: Recording

spends.description: Whether it costs money to take.
spends.title: Spends

priced_by.description: For a step that spends: the catalogue action that prices it before it is taken.
priced_by.title: Priced By

no_action.description: Why no catalogue action takes it: for no_action, why no act closes it; for an act no one action takes, or no sequence has been shown to finish, why not.
no_action.title: No Action

limits.description: What following the step as written cannot guarantee. unpaired_arms: an arm that differs from the control beyond its model would run in a launch call of its own, whose new cases the control does not run; a contrast pairs only the cases both sides ran, so such runs add no pair to it (unpaired_arms names each). A step whose caveat reads a contrast on this report launches no such arm, and makes no call where no arm it names is left beside the control (no_action lift_not_shown); a confirmation launches it, and the planned size does not hold for it. A gate or a figure reads each arm's own cases, so its step names none. axis_may_not_generate: n_variations writes unseen cases only on a template axis a model writes (llm); on an axis of stated values (enum, sample) a launch reuses stored cases with the same values and keeps fewer where they run out, and a kind that generates none refuses it. The reading holds no template's axes, so the cases are new only where the launch reports reused 0 and kept the planned count; for a confirmation, unseen cases on such an axis are authored first. this_report_stays_flagged: the caveat is read off this report's own results (a criterion set after them, a pick among them), which nothing added anywhere lifts; the confirmation is read in the campaign the step creates, and that reading is the one to trust. control_may_read_late: the control is named from a launched run, which exists only once the launch starts; named after the first result is scored, the created campaign reads its control as named late.
limits.title: Limits

unpaired_arms.description: For limits unpaired_arms: the arms whose new cases no call of the control's runs, by id: launched in a call of their own on a confirmation, not launched on a step that reads this report's contrast.
unpaired_arms.title: Unpaired Arms

RemedyStep.title: RemedyStep

StateOf.description:
The state of one reading, contrast, interval or pair, where it is not simply counted.

A holder with none reads ``counted``. The three fields are checked together (:func:`check_state`) when the value is
built and when a stored one is read, so no document holds a reason outside its state's set.

reason.description: Why it is not counted; none for counted.

coordinate.description: The coordinate a split is on, or the one an unrecorded identity names.
